# Tab drags inside a popup vessel only resort: no dock zones, no tear-out

## Context

Found in manual testing of `apps/workstation` on `dev` (2026-10-22). Tear one tab out into a popup, move a second tab into that popup, then drag the tab headers inside it:

1. **No docking.** A drag inside the popup only ever resorts the strip. No dock drop zones appear, so the popup's own layout cannot be docked into.
2. **No tear-out.** Dragging a tab out of the popup often does not tear out. The tab-header proxy is clamped to the popup's boundary. This does not happen every time.

@tobiu's screen recording shows both.

## Measurements: the live session, read-only over the Neural Link

Session `1d9d302d…` (a fresh load), main window `59069496…`, popup `d100e2b4…` (320×269, tabs "Metrics ⠿" and "Audit"). Nothing was mutated.

| sort zone | window | `allowOverdrag` | `enableProxyToPopup` | `dockGroupNodeId` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `neo-dock-tab-sortzone-1` … `-6` (all main strips) | main | `true` | `true` | `null` |
| **`neo-dock-tab-sortzone-7`** (the popup's strip) | popup | **`false`** | **`false`** | `workstation-vessel-tabs:metrics` |

The popup workspace `neo-dock-workspace-5` is a `Workstation.view.PopupWorkspace` with `enableDockTearOutLifecycle: false`. Its `getDockProjectionOptions()` returns only `{workspaceId, crossWindowSortGroup, enableStackDrag: true}`.

## The Problem

The popup's strip is projected without the drag contract the main window's strips get:

- `LayoutAdapter` arms `allowOverdrag` and `enableProxyToPopup` only for `context.enableDockTearOut === true`. Without them the proxy is clamped to its boundary and the tear-out exit can never fire, as the adapter's own comment says.
- `Neo.dashboard.dock.Workspace#getDockProjectionOptions()` returns `{}` unless `enableDockTearOutLifecycle` is on. `PopupWorkspace` keeps that off, because the root workspace owns the vessel lifecycle. Its override spreads `super` correctly, but `super` has nothing to give.
- `VesselWorkspace`, the main window, also wires `onDockCrossZoneDragMove` / `onDockCrossZoneDragCancel` to its `dragAffordances`, plus `dockTearOutBoundaryContainerId` and `enableVesselConversion`. `PopupWorkspace` publishes none of them, so a drag inside the popup paints no drop zones.

**Why "not always", inferred and not traced:** the popup still publishes `crossWindowSortGroup`, so a drag that ends over another Workstation window can be carried there by the cross-window coordinator. Over empty desktop the clamped proxy has no way out.

The engine guard from #18197 / #18199, which refuses a context that dropped the tear-out opt-ins, does not fire here. It only checks workspaces whose tear-out lifecycle is on.

## The Architectural Reality

- `apps/workstation/view/PopupWorkspace.mjs`: `getDockProjectionOptions()` (identity only), `getDockParticipationConfig()` (the root's proxy embodiment, and a hit-test that admits drops only while populated).
- `apps/workstation/view/VesselWorkspace.mjs`: `getDockProjectionOptions()`, the full contract the popup lacks.
- `src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs` `getDockProjectionOptions()`, and `src/dashboard/dock/projection/LayoutAdapter.mjs` (the sort-zone flags).
- **Design authority:** the product intent recorded in #19248. Dragging inside a popup should *"feel the same like dragging a tab inside a main window"*, because *"popups can have a big size and their own dock layout"*. Its three-phase model: a tab-header proxy in an app, a popup outside apps, a tab-header proxy again on re-entering an app.

## The Fix

Give the popup's strips the main window's drag contract, delegated to the root that owns the vessel lifecycle:

- the tear-out opt-in and gesture callbacks from `rootWorkspace.tearOutHandlers.getProjectionCallbacks()`;
- the popup's own `dockTearOutBoundaryContainerId: me.id`;
- `enableVesselConversion`;
- drop-zone affordance callbacks (`onDockCrossZoneDragMove` / `…Cancel`) for the popup's dock host.

The whole-stack drag (`enableStackDrag`, the ⠿ handle) and the populated-only hit-test stay as they are.

**Trap.** A tear-out from a popup is a second `window.open` under the same held gesture only if the drag already rode a vessel. Use the same admission path main uses, which already handles the one-popup-per-activation constraint (#19533), rather than opening windows from the popup directly.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A popup's tab-strip zones carry `allowOverdrag: true` and `enableProxyToPopup: true`, the same as main's.
- [ ] Dragging a popup tab within the popup shows the dock's drop previews over the popup's dock host, and dropping commits the same operations a main-window drop would.
- [ ] Dragging a popup tab out of the popup over empty desktop tears it out into a new popup every time, instead of clamping to the popup's boundary.
- [ ] The whole-stack drag via the ⠿ handle behaves as today.
- [ ] **E2E:** a new whitebox Neural Link spec, `test/playwright/e2e/workstation/WorkstationPopupTabDragNL.spec.mjs`, uses the existing tear-out helpers. It tears out a tab, moves a second tab into that popup, then asserts (a) a drop preview appears for a drag inside the popup and (b) a drag out of the popup admits a new vessel. It must be red on `dev` (resort-only, clamped) and green with the fix, and it joins the hosted Workstation NL tier (#19655).
